answer: An agent market can require each trading identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid, much as each boat needs a paid berth at a jetty. Creating 10,000 identities then ties up $1 million, imposing financing costs even if every bond is returned. The rule offers no ivory tower guarantee against wealthy attackers, but it prevents cheap account creation from turning the market into a haven for sybils.
